description:
Read .lattice/notes/design-decisions-2026-07-04.md first. It binds this task.

Write the measurement design doc the release skill (DB-8) and every run follows. Cover:

- the headline metric: per-model sensitivity score, defined as the paired accuracy drop against the canonical dialect over the frozen suite
- paired design: same forms through every dialect, within-item comparison, McNemar tests, bootstrap confidence intervals over items
- suite freezing: suite v1 fixes dialects, forms and seeds; scores always report per suite version
- sampling: one sample per (form, dialect, model); document the retirement of the old k=3, 4-expressions-per-sample, all-pass design and why scores break across that change
- sample size: confidence interval maths and a power argument for the paired design; concrete n per cell
- model grid, 4 tiers: cheap closed (full suite), 2 to 3 flagships (frozen core), open-weight via OpenRouter, reasoning-toggle pairs
- a worked budget sheet showing a full release run within 100 US dollars, stretch 150, using batch APIs at half price and gating visual dialects to cheap multimodal models first
- open questions section: prompt anchoring (parens examples in the system prompt; mixed brackets like [()] outperform (()); notation-neutral prompts make models default to parens) as a candidate ablation

Ground cost numbers in observed token usage from logs/ and notebooks/data-history, not guesses. Reconcile with notebooks/measurement.org. Put the doc where DB-8 can cite it (suggest docs/).
title: Measurement design doc: sensitivity score, frozen suite v1, budget sheet
